newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power continues to firm on cold.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power continues to firm on cold.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. continued their week-long climb Thursday, rising about $25 from a week ago, supported by colder weather in the region and stronger gas prices, sources said.

Firm, peak power prices in the northern part of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Friday were firmer again in the $39.00-41.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, as compared with Wednesday's $36.00-37.00 trading range.
Firm, off-peak electricity in northern TVA was notionally assessed at $16.00-19.00, but most traders said they were not pre-scheduling any off-peak power.
At the Georgia/Florida border, prices for firm, peak electricity in 16 hour blocks for Friday delivery were discussed in the $42.00-43.00 range, up from Wednesday's $40.00-41.00 trading range.
Firm, off-peak power for Friday at the Ga./Fla. border was still notionally assessed at $15.50-16.00.

In Florida, where most daytime highs in the north have slipped into the 40s and 50s Fahrenheit and lows are in the teens, peak power prices on a 16-hour schedule for Friday were talked at $45.00 and higher, but most traders were hesitant to schedule any power.

"We're not scheduling anything for tomorrow. We're not taking any chances. We're going to trade everything on an hourly basis," one trader said, noting several combustion and diesel units were on hold if needed.
Temperatures in the region are expected to be about 10 to 20 degrees below-normal through the end of the week, with slightly milder temperatures expected for the weekend.
Another cold front is expected to move across the eastern U.S. by late next week.
Like power prices, natural gas spot values in south Texas rose by about 10 cents today to the about $4.60 per million British thermal units.
